articles.title: Actor Laith Nakli Faces Deportation Fight as His Biggest Film Opens
articles.excerpt: The 56-year-old Manhattan actor's immigration case, closed in 2013, was reopened this year — one of nearly 150,000 sent back to court since January 2025 — as his film with Mahershala Ali wins critical attention.
articles.image_caption: Laith Nakli is reflected in a mirror at his home in New York in September 2026. His immigration case, closed in 2013, was reopened this year as his film with Mahershala Ali opens.
articles.nri_angle: Nakli's case turns on administrative closure — a mechanism many long-settled immigrants in the US relied on — and its reopening shows how a decades-old plea can resurface.
tags: your mother your mother your mother
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Nakli pleads guilty to drug charges

articles.title: Trump Says Deportation Policy Was 'Too Tough' in Post-Midterm Interview
articles.excerpt: In his first sit-down since the Republican midterm defeat, President Trump told 60 Minutes removals of workers with good jobs hurt his party — an hour after recording, he replaced his chief of staff with the policy's architect, Stephen Miller.
articles.image_caption: President Donald Trump speaks in the Oval Office of the White House in Washington. In a 60 Minutes interview aired on November 8, Trump said his deportation policy was too tough.
articles.nri_angle: No rule, fee or filing changed with the interview — for Indian families in the US immigration system, the practical position is unchanged until Congress or the agencies act.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Alberta Invites 425 Workers in Five Provincial Immigration Draws
articles.excerpt: The Alberta Advantage Immigration Program issued 425 invitations across five draws between October 23 and November 2, led by the Rural Renewal Stream — but only 495 of the province's 6,603 nomination spaces for 2026 remain.
articles.image_caption: The Alberta Legislature Building in Edmonton, in an official Government of Alberta image. The province issued 425 AAIP invitations across five draws between October 23 and November 2.

sources.label: Government of Alberta — AAIP Processing Information

articles.nri_angle: Alberta's draws are a live route to Canadian permanent residence for Indian workers already in Canada or with job offers in designated rural communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

steps.detail: An invitation is not a nomination. Invited candidates apply to the Alberta Advantage Immigration Program for a provincial nomination.
If AAIP approves the application, it issues a nomination. The process can take several months, and Alberta had 495 of its 6,603 nomination spaces for 2026 still remaining as of November 4.

steps.step: Apply to the federal government for permanent residence
steps.detail: Nominees apply to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada for PR. Express Entry nominees receive 600 additional CRS points, which in practice guarantees a federal invitation.
Nominees already in Canada who have submitted a PR application may qualify for a Bridging Open Work Permit while they wait.

data_cards.title: Invited by AAIP? What Happens Next

articles.title: BJP Attacks Sonia Gandhi Over Babri Remark in Memoir Interviews
articles.excerpt: BJP spokesmen Sudhanshu Trivedi and Pradeep Bhandari accused Congress of an 'anti-Ram' face after Sonia Gandhi said she cried watching the 1992 Babri Masjid demolition, days before her memoir 'Belonging' is published on November 10.
articles.image_caption: The Babri Masjid in Ayodhya. The mosque was demolished on December 6, 1992, at the site that is now home to the Ram temple.
articles.nri_angle: The Ayodhya dispute remains one of the most closely followed stories in Indian politics for the diaspora, and the memoir-driven exchange revives it days before the book's November 10 release.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Australia Student Visa Changes Split Families and Force Offshore Applications
articles.excerpt: Rules in force since 2 October 2026 bar most students from including family, abolish adding family after grant with no exemptions, and push further applications offshore — leaving students whose visas expire mid-course, and families planning to reunite, with hard deadlines.

sources.label: Law Council of Australia (Department of Home Affairs advice)
Australian Department of Home Affairs — Including or adding family members

articles.nri_angle: India is neither a Pacific nor an ASEAN country, so most Indian students in Australia can include family only via the PhD, DFAT/Defence sponsorship or fully funded foreign government scholarship exemptions — and with onshore applications largely closed and family additions after grant abolished, Indian families must settle study, spouse and childcare plans before the first application is lodged.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

Target net overseas migration by mid-2028

articles.title: UK Budget 2026: Lower Going Rates, Two-Year Graduate Visa for Some
articles.excerpt: The Budget promises 25th-percentile going rates from spring 2027, a two-year Graduate visa for graduates of qualifying universities, and an HPI route widened to the top 150 institutions — but the general threshold will rise, the PhD discount will go, and most detail is still unpublished.

sources.label: Hill Dickinson — Immigration changes hidden in the 2026 Budget
Paragon Law — UK Autumn Budget 2026 immigration changes

articles.nri_angle: Indians are among the largest cohorts on the UK's Skilled Worker, Graduate and HPI routes, so the spring 2027 move to 25th-percentile going rates, the two-year Graduate visa for qualifying universities, and the HPI expansion to the top 150 institutions directly shape whether Indian graduates can stay, switch and settle in Britain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Visa Curbs Push Indian IT Firms Toward Offshore Hiring, Analysts Say
articles.excerpt: Washington has frozen green card sponsorship at eight major employers and attached a $100,000 payment to many new H-1B hires from abroad, and analysts say the industry's response is to move the job to India rather than the worker to America.
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals account for over 70 percent of approved H-1B petitions, so the PERM freeze at four Indian-headquartered firms and the $100,000 payment on hires from abroad land directly on Indian engineers mid-queue for green cards — while analysts say the work itself is increasingly likely to be offered in Bengaluru, Hyderabad or Pune instead of on site in the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Manitoba Invites 526 Workers in Draw 283, Led by Manufacturing and Farm Jobs
articles.excerpt: The province's 22nd draw of 2026 sent 448 of its 526 Letters of Advice to Apply to people already working in Manitoba in natural resources, agriculture, manufacturing and utilities, with 60 days to file a full nomination application.
articles.image_caption: An aerial view of a Manitoba community at sunset. Manitoba Draw #283 issued 526 Letters of Advice to Apply on November 5, 2026, most of them to workers already employed in the province.
articles.nri_angle: Indian workers already employed in Manitoba's agriculture, manufacturing and utilities sectors were the target of this draw; invitees have 60 days to file a complete nomination application.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.text: Submit a complete MPNP nomination application within 60 days of your Letter of Advice to Apply

items.note: The MPNP may refuse applications that cannot show this
items.text: If you work in a regulated occupation, be able to prove you are fully licensed to work in Manitoba
After nomination, you can request an MPNP work permit support letter for a federal work permit application
Once you have applied for permanent residence, you may be eligible for a bridging open work permit

articles.title: Canada Names the Pathways Behind Its 200,000 Extra PR Spaces for 2027
articles.excerpt: IRCC will fill the one-time 2027 spaces from applications already in the system: provincial nominee workers and closed economic programs in one cohort of 100,000, and family and humanitarian cases in the other.
articles.image_caption: The flag of Canada. IRCC has named the pathways that will fill 200,000 additional in-Canada permanent residence spaces in 2027.
articles.nri_angle: Indians are among the largest groups of temporary residents in Canada; anyone with a pending PNP, caregiver, closed-program or in-Canada spousal application is in line for the extra 2027 processing space, with no new application needed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.text: Workers eligible for permanent residence through the Provincial Nominee Program (outside Quebec)
Applicants waiting under the closed Start-up Visa and Self-Employed Persons programs
Applicants waiting under the Agri-Food Pilot and home care worker pathways
Spouses, common-law partners and children of Canadians and permanent residents who have already applied
Hong Kong and Ukraine family pathway applicants with applications still in the system
Humanitarian and compassionate applicants approved in principle

data_cards.title: Who the 2027 Measure Covers
data_cards.catch_text: No new intake opens with this measure — it processes applications already submitted, and no separate application is needed.

articles.title: Democrats Won Congress. For H-1B Holders, the Rules Still Run Through Agencies and Courts
articles.excerpt: Almost every H-1B and PERM restriction since September 2025 came from the White House and federal agencies — and a midterm win does not repeal an agency rule.
articles.image_caption: An Indian passport sits beside H-1B visa paperwork in front of a US flag and the USCIS website. Democrats winning Congress leaves the H-1B rulebook with federal agencies and the courts.
articles.nri_angle: Indian professionals hold 71% of approved H-1B petitions; this explains exactly what the new Congress can and cannot change for them, and by when.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Waives $25 OCI Passport-Update Penalty Until December 31, 2026
articles.excerpt: It is a one-time waiver, not a removal: late updates received between November 1 and December 31 escape the $25 penalty, which returns on January 1, 2027.
articles.image_caption: An Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card (file photo). India has waived the 5 passport-update penalty until December 31, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: Any OCI holder who renewed a foreign passport more than three months ago can file the overdue update free until December 31, 2026 — after that the $25 penalty applies again.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: One-time $25 late-update penalty waiver window opens for updates received from this date
Waiver window closes — last day to file a late passport update without the penalty

steps.detail: If your new foreign passport was issued more than 3 months ago and you have not updated it on your OCI record, you are in the group the waiver covers.

steps.step: File the update on the e-OCI portal
steps.detail: Submit the passport-particulars update online before December 31, 2026; the waiver covers updates received in the window.
The Government of India has clarified that OCI holders can travel to and from India while a delayed passport update is under process.

articles.title: Judge Blocks Trump's 250-Foot Washington Arch Hours After Panel Approves It
articles.excerpt: Judge Tanya Chutkan paused all construction at Memorial Circle for 14 days after the planning commission's 8-4 approval, in the fight over whether Congress ever authorised the monument.
articles.nri_angle: The ruling freezes a contested change to the monumental core of Washington, DC, a city where many Indian-Americans work in federal service and visit Arlington and the Lincoln Memorial.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Judge blocks construction of the arch.
Administration must certify compliance to the court.
DC and Virginia filed a lawsuit against the arch.

articles.title: Canada Holds PR Target at 380,000, Opens Path for 200,000 Already There
articles.excerpt: The 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan keeps admissions flat at 380,000 a year, but Budget 2026 adds a one-time transition to permanent residence for up to 200,000 temporary residents already in Canada by the end of 2027.
articles.image_caption: Parliament Hill in Ottawa. Canada's 2027-2029 Immigration Levels Plan, released with Budget 2026, holds permanent resident admissions at 380,000 a year.
articles.nri_angle: For Indians in Canada on work or study permits, the one-time transition for people already in the country is the one new opening in an otherwise flat plan.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Tightens Nepal, Bhutan Border Rules: Passport Now Needed for Third-Country Travel
articles.excerpt: A Home Ministry amendment keeps direct India–Nepal and India–Bhutan travel passport-free but makes a Visa Manual identity document mandatory at immigration — and closes the route for using either neighbour as a passport-free bridge to a third country.

sources.label: The Times of India via 7Globe — Centre amends Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) Order: What Indians travelling to or returning from Nepal or Bhutan need to know
ANI via NewKerala — MHA Amends Immigration Order, Identity Documents Mandatory for India-Nepal-Bhutan Travel
PTI via News89 — Govt Relaxes Passport, Visa Norms For Select Foreigners, Refugees Living In India

articles.nri_angle: Indians and NRIs who visit family or transit through Nepal and Bhutan must now show a specified identity document, and anyone routing to a third country through either border needs a passport and a designated immigration post.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DeSantis Blames Midterm Rout on GOP Failure to 'Shut Off H-1B Visas'
articles.excerpt: Florida's governor called the Republican defeat 'close to an extinction-level event' and faulted Senate Republicans for not ending the H-1B programme — the route used by most Indian tech professionals in the US — while they held Congress.

sources.label: BizzBuzz — Florida Governor calls Midterm rout 'close to extinction-level event', says Republicans failed to 'shut off H-1B visas'
Nation Press — DeSantis calls midterm losses 'extinction-level event', faults GOP on H-1B visas
Fox News — DeSantis calls GOP midterm losses 'extinction-level event' — and explains why Florida survived

articles.nri_angle: DeSantis's call to shut off H-1B targets a programme whose approved petitions are 70 per cent India-born; a Democratic Congress makes that legislation unlikely near term.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Republicans lost control of both the House and Senate
New H-1B petition fee applies for certain applicants

articles.title: Lawyers Say Midterm Result Brings No Immediate H-1B Relief
articles.excerpt: Immigration lawyers and analysts say the new Congress can scrutinise H-1B restrictions and block tighter bills, but the fee, the weighted lottery and green-card dates all sit outside a simple election result.

sources.label: The Hindu BusinessLine — Visa policies remain uncertain for Indian IT firms
GC EB-1 — Democrats Win Congress: What It Means, and What It Cannot Change, for Indians on H-1B Visas

articles.nri_angle: For the Indian professionals who receive most H-1B approvals, the lawyer consensus is to plan on current fees, weighted selection and bulletin dates rather than expect post-election relief.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: No Aadhaar? NRI Students Can Apply for JEE Main 2027 With Passport
articles.excerpt: The NTA says NRI applicants without Aadhaar, PAN or an Indian driving licence can enter passport details instead — fresh applications without a late fee close November 22, 2026.
articles.image_caption: An exam answer sheet, calculator and study books in a JEE Main 2027 graphic. NRI students without an Aadhaar card can now apply for JEE Main 2027 using a passport.

sources.label: Jagran Josh — No Aadhaar? NRI Students Can Now Apply for JEE Main 2027 Using Passport
Disha Stars — JEE Main 2027: NRI Candidates Without Aadhaar or PAN Can Apply Using Passport
Careers360 — MeriPehchan Mandatory for JEE Main Registration Process 2027

articles.nri_angle: Overseas Indian students can now register for India's main engineering entrance exam with the passport they hold abroad, instead of being blocked by missing domestic ID documents.

articles.title: SEBI Finalises Digital KYC From Abroad for NRIs, Effective December 3
articles.excerpt: A final SEBI circular dated November 4 replaces the August proposal: eligible NRIs, OCIs and foreign nationals in FATF-compliant countries can onboard digitally from overseas, with portable KYC records.

sources.label: TaxGuru — SEBI circular dated November 4, 2026 (HO/38/30/12(3)2026-MIRSD-POD2/I/25175/2026), full text
FinBrooks — SEBI Eases Digital KYC Rules for NRIs, Foreign Nationals From December 3
IANS via The Freedom Press — SEBI allows digital KYC for overseas investors without physical presence in India

articles.nri_angle: NRIs and OCIs will no longer need a trip to India or a couriered paper file to open or renew an Indian investment account, if they live in an FATF-compliant country.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India to Cut Visa Form Fields by Around 70% in Overhaul for Foreign Travellers
articles.excerpt: The Home Ministry plans slimmer forms across all 22 visa categories from next year, dropping the 'district' field and letting tourists list a hotel as their local address.
articles.nri_angle: Simpler Indian visa paperwork for foreign-national relatives, spouses and friends of the diaspora planning trips to India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Survey: Most Microsoft India Staff Report Hikes Of Five Percent Or Less
articles.excerpt: A Blind survey of 2,178 India-based professionals found 91% of Microsoft respondents reporting hikes of 5% or less — self-reported figures that arrive alongside a voluntary buyout offer to about 60,000 employees.
articles.image_caption: An aerial view shows Microsoft's West Campus in Redmond, Washington. A Blind survey found 91% of Microsoft India respondents received pay hikes of 5% or less this year.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian tech workers in India and the diaspora, the survey captures pay anxiety arriving at the same time as a large voluntary exit offer at one of the sector's biggest employers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UK Doubles Settlement Wait to Ten Years, Keeps Five-Year Route for Care Workers
articles.excerpt: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood's earned-settlement plan doubles the standard ILR wait from five years to ten, applied retrospectively — but care workers earning at least £25,000 who met their visa conditions, higher earners, and many public sector workers keep a five-year route.
articles.image_caption: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood leaves 10 Downing Street in London. The government plans to double the qualifying wait for permanent settlement to ten years, while care workers keep a five-year route if they meet visa and earnings conditions.
articles.nri_angle: Indians are one of the largest groups on UK work and health and care visas, so the doubled ten-year default — and the care-worker and salary carve-outs — directly change settlement timelines for thousands of Indian families in Britain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ICE Officer Indicted in Houston Had Been on Job Just Over a Year
articles.excerpt: Mario Alberto Morales, a 2025 surge hire, surrendered Monday on an aggravated-assault indictment over an October 10 vehicle strike in Houston. He denies wrongdoing, ICE calls the case a political stunt — and his hiring record is now part of the story.
articles.nri_angle: The case tests how the rapid expansion of ICE's workforce is vetted and trained — a question with direct consequences for immigrant communities, including Indian nationals, facing enforcement.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.text: Officer Morales indicted on October 10 incident.
Victim Miguel Parra Hernandez suffered multiple leg fractures.
Next court hearing scheduled for December 2.

articles.title: 'The Boat's Sunk': Kansas City Immigration Court Buried Under 40,000 Cases
articles.excerpt: Attorneys in Kansas City warn that the only immigration court serving Missouri and Kansas is overwhelmed by a backlog KMBC puts at about 40,000 cases — with too few judges and too few lawyers for the people waiting on hearings.

sources.label: US Department of Justice, EOIR — Kansas City Immigration Court

articles.nri_angle: Indian and other immigrant families in Missouri and Kansas wait in this single court's queue for asylum and removal decisions, often without a lawyer.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 66 Lawmakers Urge Trump Administration to Halt Afghan Deportation Flights
articles.excerpt: A bicameral letter led by Rep. Scott Peters asks Secretaries Rubio and Mullin to cancel flights that would send at least 150 Afghans from Louisiana to Pakistan — with Afghanistan, an ICE officer's court declaration says, the intended final destination.
articles.nri_angle: South Asian readers with Afghan family, colleagues or community ties face a live removal operation this week; the congressional letter is the main public challenge to it so far.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.label: Afghans planned for deportation through Pakistan

articles.title: Tennessee DACA Recipients Sue Over Driver's Licenses Denied Under New Law
articles.excerpt: A law that took effect October 1 requires a federally authorized period of stay for a temporary license — a test DACA recipients and some work-permit holders no longer pass. Advocates sued on October 30 to block it.
articles.nri_angle: Indian and other immigrant residents of Tennessee on work permits should check whether their temporary license renewal is affected before it expires.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
